transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. To start, can you tell me what's been bothering you or what brought you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Well, I guess what finally brought me in is that I just don't feel like myself anymore. 

I used to always make time for things I enjoyed—painting, hiking, singing in my choir, and our Sunday family gatherings. But lately... even when I have a free hour, I just sit there. I just find myself completely unable to care about any of it.
How long have you been feeling this way—unable to enjoy or care about the things you used to love?

I'd say it's been building for about eight months now. Um, it seemed to start right around the time I took over the STEM-Arts curriculum initiative at work. Since then, it's just kind of been this way.
Over these past eight months, have you also been feeling sad, empty, or down most of the day, nearly every day?

Yes, I have. Um, most days it just feels like there's a heavy gray film over everything. I can be standing right there in a classroom full of students, or at home with my husband, and I still just feel... hollow. And really close to tears, honestly.
Have you ever gone through a period like this before—weeks or months of feeling this down and disconnected—at any earlier point in your life?
No, I haven't. I mean, I've had stressful weeks before, or just normal sad days, but... nothing like this. This is really the first time I've ever felt this down for this long.
Have you been diagnosed with any medical illnesses, started any new medications, or had any significant changes in your physical health around the time these feelings began?
No, nothing like that. I haven't had any new health problems, and I'm not taking any new medications. Physically, everything seems pretty much the same as it always has been.
Have you noticed any changes in your sleep—such as trouble falling asleep, staying asleep, or sleeping much more than usual—since this started?

Yes, my sleep has been really messed up lately. Um, for months now, actually. I'll just lie awake at night, and my brain won't shut off—I just keep replaying all these details about the school grants I help manage. And then, even if I do fall asleep, I almost always wake up around three or four in the morning and can't get back to sleep. Even on the rare nights where I sleep a bit longer, I wake up feeling like I didn't rest at all.
Have you been experiencing feelings of worthlessness or excessive guilt about yourself over these past several months?

Yes, I have. Um, especially at work. Whenever anything goes wrong with the curriculum project I help with—even if it's just something really small—I keep thinking that I'm completely letting the students down. And... I don't know, I just get this overwhelming feeling that I'm wasting all the sacrifices my parents made for me to even have this kind of opportunity in the first place. I just feel awful about it all the time.
Have you had any thoughts of death, or thoughts that you'd be better off dead, or thoughts of harming yourself during this time?

Yes, I have. Um... on those late nights when I'm working in the studio, I sometimes catch myself thinking that it would just be a relief if I didn't wake up. I haven't made a plan to do anything, but... well, those thoughts really scare me. They scared me enough that I finally told my husband about it, because I realized I couldn't keep handling them alone.
Given everything you've described, are you still able to go to work and manage your daily responsibilities, or has this made it very difficult to function in your day-to-day life?

It's... it's definitely made things very difficult. I've actually missed several of my teaching sessions lately. I just... I've been avoiding the student workshops, too, because I simply can't keep up with the responsibilities the way I used to. It's too overwhelming. And at home, it's the same. My husband has really had to step in a lot more. I find myself just withdrawing from our family plans, and... I just don't feel safe trying to push through all of this alone anymore.
